name: Kettlebell Transverse Lunge
description:
A lunge in the transverse (rotational) plane rather than forward, back, or sideways. **The bell stays racked on the working side the whole time — it does not swing and it does not drop.** Pivot on the stance foot and sweep the trailing leg back and across at an angle, letting the torso rotate open with it, sinking until the back knee is low and the back heel is up; the free arm reaches forward as a counterbalance. Drive out of it back to standing. The rotation is the point — the offset rack load fights the twist, so the obliques and the stance hip control a plane most lunges never touch. Harder to stabilize than a forward or lateral lunge: go light, go slow, and don't let the racked shoulder get pulled forward.

**Finish in the inside rack.** As you stand, settle the bell into a tight rack threaded up the INSIDE line — elbow in against the ribs, bell resting on the forearm, shoulder packed down. In a flow this landing is what the next move launches from, so it's a position to hit deliberately, not somewhere you happen to end up.
